title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in E410 Euler sets up general equilibrium and motion equations for a plane line. The line may be perfectly flexible or elastic. The variables are arc length s, abscissa x, ordinate y, and the angle Φ. Here cos Φ = dy/ds, so Φ is measured from the y-axis. The internal forces are a tangential tension T and a normal (shear) force V. The bending moment is S·dΦ/ds, where S is the elastic stiffness. Σ is the line density ('crassities'), and Σ/2g plays the role of mass, since 2g is the acceleration of gravity in Euler's units. On the previous page he eliminated the moment arm and obtained V = S Φ'' + S' Φ'. He then reduced the general system to two equations (I: tangential, II: normal) for the special case of small vibrations.

On this page, string case (§XLII). He linearizes: y is infinitely small, x ≈ s, Φ ≈ 90°, sin Φ = 1, cos Φ = 0, and ∂x/∂t = ∂²x/∂t² = 0.
- Equation I gives ∂T/∂s = 0, so T is constant in s. He adds the explicit assumption that it also stays constant in time.
- Differentiating cos Φ = y_s gives -Φ_s sin Φ = y_ss, so Φ_s = -y_ss.
- Equation II (T Φ_s = -(Σ/2g) y_tt sin Φ) then becomes A y_ss = (Σ/2g) y_tt, where A is the tension.
- He identifies this as the equation 'the authors' (d'Alembert, Euler, D. Bernoulli, Lagrange) used for vibrating strings. With variable Σ(s) it is the inhomogeneous string equation.

Elastic lamina (§XLIII). The same linearization is used and external forces P, Q are dropped. The previous formula becomes V = -S'(s) y_ss - S y_sss = -(S y_ss)_s, the shear force of a beam of variable stiffness. The two remaining equations are:
- T_s - V y_ss = 0
- V_s + T y_ss = (Σ/2g) y_tt

On the next page, for uniform stiffness S = A, V = -A y_sss. Integrating T_s = -A y_ss y_sss gives T = B - (A/2) y_ss². Eliminating T then yields a fourth-order equation: -A y_ssss + (B - (A/2) y_ss²) y_ss = (Σ/2g) y_tt. To linear order this is the Euler–Bernoulli beam equation with axial tension B, i.e. a stiff string. It reduces to the classical bar equation when B = 0 and to the string equation when A = 0.

Purpose: to show that the new general theory contains both the known string equation and the known elastic-bar vibration equation as special cases.
errors: The vanishing of ∂x/∂t is stated as if it followed from x ≈ s. It is really part of the small-amplitude (purely transverse motion) assumption.
Constancy of tension in time is an extra hypothesis, which Euler acknowledges ('siquidem ... supponitur'). Equation I gives only ∂T/∂s = 0.

Mild inconsistency in the beam case (completed on the next page). The term T = B - (A/2) y_ss² keeps a second-order quantity, while second-order terms were discarded elsewhere (sin Φ = 1, cos Φ = 0, x_t = 0). The cubic term y_ss³ in the resulting equation is therefore not consistently derived. To consistent linear order T = B.

ideas.what: Recovery of the vibrating-string equation A y_ss = (Σ/2g) y_tt from general equations for a flexible line, with possibly variable density
ideas.where_published: Euler E119/E140 and later string papers; here as a special case in E410

ideas.what: Shear force of a laminated beam with variable stiffness, V = -(S y'')'
ideas.modern_name: shear force–moment relation, Euler–Bernoulli beam with variable flexural rigidity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler / D. Bernoulli (1730s–1740s); general equations analysed in Truesdell's commentary on E410
ideas.where_published: E410; discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera Omnia II.11.2)

ideas.what: Linearized transverse balance V' + T y'' = ρ y_tt coupled with tangential balance T' - V y'' = 0
ideas.modern_name: beam under axial tension (stiff string); balance of linear momentum with tension and shear
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E410 is credited by Truesdell as the first general dynamic theory of the elastic line)

ideas.what: Tension varying along a uniform vibrating lamina as T = B - (A/2) y''^2
ideas.modern_name: nonlinear coupling of axial force and curvature (geometrically exact rod, small-curvature expansion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; modern nonlinear rod theory (Kirchhoff, Antman)

deep.surprise_reason: The page reduces Euler's general flexible/elastic-line equations to the known string and beam equations. E410 and these reductions are analysed in detail by Truesdell in Opera Omnia II.11.2. The tension-curvature formula on the next page is mildly interesting, but it is inconsistently derived and already in the record.
transcription_corrections: Previous page: 'motum cordatum vibrantium' should read 'motum cordarum vibrantium'.

Equation I on the previous page is stated in the printed context as ∂T/∂s = ...; this page's reduction (cos Φ = 0, x_tt = 0) is consistent with the image. No significant errors found in this page's transcription.
